title: Cassandra Small Examples
description: Use these small Cassandra examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Create a local practice keyspace
examples.description: A keyspace groups Cassandra tables and defines replication.
examples.code:
CREATE KEYSPACE IF NOT EXISTS cma_reading WITH replication = {'class':'SimpleStrategy','replication_factor':1};
USE cma_reading;
examples.output: The local practice keyspace uses one replica.

examples.title: Design a table for one question
examples.description: The partition key chooses a group of rows stored together.
examples.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_reader(reader_id text,day date,title text,pages int,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id),day)) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY(day DESC);
examples.output: The table groups a reader's entries by reader_id and orders that reader's days newest first.

examples.title: Insert a reading entry
examples.description: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address.
examples.output: Mia's entry for that day stores Moon Trip and 20 pages.

examples.title: Read one partition
examples.description: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key.
examples.code: SELECT day,title,pages FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia';
examples.output: The query returns Mia's stored days in the table's clustering order.

examples.title: Read a range inside a partition
examples.description: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column.
examples.code: SELECT day,title FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day>='2026-11-01' LIMIT 5;
examples.output: At most five of Mia's entries from the chosen date range are returned.

examples.title: Keep partitions a manageable size
examples.description: A partition should not grow without a useful bound.
examples.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_month(reader_id text,month text,day date,title text,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id,month),day));
examples.output: The partition key now combines a reader and a month, such as mia with 2026-11.

examples.title: Expire temporary fields
examples.description: A TTL gives written values a time to live.
examples.code:
INSERT INTO reading_by_reader(reader_id,day,title,pages) VALUES('temporary-reader','2026-11-16','Practice',1) USING TTL 60;
SELECT TTL(title) FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='temporary-reader' AND day='2026-11-16';
examples.output: The TTL value is near 60 seconds when read immediately and decreases with time.

examples.title: Update by the full key
examples.description: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values.
examples.code: UPDATE reading_by_reader SET pages=25 WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day='2026-11-16';
examples.output: The page count at that exact reader-and-day address becomes 25.

examples.title: Delete one known row
examples.description: A DELETE marks selected data as deleted.
examples.code: DELETE FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='temporary-reader' AND day='2026-11-16';
examples.output: The named temporary sample entry is no longer returned by normal reads.

examples.title: Group a small related write
examples.description: A batch can group related mutations. It is not a general speed trick for sending many unrelated partitions at once.
examples.output: Both changes target the same practice row in one partition.

examples.title: Use a dedicated counter table
examples.description: Cassandra counters use a special column type and update rules.
examples.output: The stored counter increases by one each time the update is applied.

examples.title: Match consistency to the cluster
examples.description: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation.
examples.code:
Worked example with three replicas:
ONE needs one replica response.
QUORUM needs a majority: two responses.
The local course has only one replica, so it cannot demonstrate surviving multiple replica failures.
examples.output: The example shows why a stronger response requirement can trade availability for stronger agreement.
